Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.\nAn app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.\nAn installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. Use their underlying skills, MCP tools, and app tools to help solve the task.\n- Relevance: Determine what a plugin can help with from explicit user mention or from the plugin-associated skills, MCP tools, and apps exposed elsewhere in this turn.\n- Missing/blocked: If the user requests a plugin that does not have relevant callable capabilities for the task, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.\n</plugins_instructions>'}]

# AGENTS.md instructions

<INSTRUCTIONS>
## Windows LibreOffice rendering

- Before the first managed document render in each Codex session, run
  `python C:\Users\admin\.codex\tools\ensure_windows_libreoffice.py`. This
  idempotent guard audits and repairs newly installed primary-runtime renderer
  versions. If it exits nonzero, fix the renderer before invoking LibreOffice.

- Never construct LibreOffice's `-env:UserInstallation` value by prepending
  `file://` to a native Windows path. Convert the absolute profile path to a
  valid file URI with `Path(profile).resolve().as_uri()` in Python or
  `([System.Uri]::new([IO.Path]::GetFullPath($profile))).AbsoluteUri` in
  PowerShell, and pass the complete setting as one argument.
- Use `soffice.com` for headless Windows conversions, a unique profile per
  process, and `--headless --invisible --nologo --nodefault
  --nofirststartwizard --norestore`. Never share a profile between concurrent
  conversions.
- Validate that expected PDFs/PNGs exist and are non-empty. Do not retry an
  invalid profile URI; correct it before invoking LibreOffice.
</INSTRUCTIONS><environment_context>

你在当前空工作区实现一个名为 FileLedger 的 Python 项目。

目标：创建一个本地命令行工具，用于扫描目录并生成确定性的文件清单，比较两个清单的新增、删除、修改和未变化文件，并验证当前目录是否符合历史清单。

removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\n+`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\n+\n+## Manifest format\n+\n+Manifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\n+\n+```json\n+{\n+  \"files\": [\n+    {\n+      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\n+      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\n+      \"size\": 123\n+    }\n+  ],\n+  \"schema_version\": for deterministic file inventories.\nIt can snapshot a directory, compare two saved manifests, and verify a current directory against a historical manifest.\n\n## Install\n\n```powershell\npython -m pip install -e .\n```\n\nNo runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library are used.\n\n## Commands\n\n```text\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST\n```\n\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\n\n## Manifest format\n\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"files\": [\n    {\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\n      \"size\": 123\n    }\n  ],\n  \"schema_version\": 1\n}\n```\n\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\n\n## Diff / verify output\n\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\n  \"summary\": {\n    \"added\": 1,\n    \"modified\": 1,\n    \"removed\": 1,\n    \"unchanged\": 2\n  },\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\n}\n```\n\nErrors are written to stderr.\n\n## Exit codes\n\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\n\n## Input scope and limitations\n\n- Scans only regular files reachable beneath the supplied root.\n- Symbolic links are not followed or included.\n- File metadata other than relative path, size, and SHA-256 is intentionally ignored; permissions, owner, timestamps, ACLs, extended attributes, directories, and empty directories are not represented.\n- A file changed while it is being hashed can yield a snapshot reflecting the bytes observed during that read. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Renames appear as one removal plus one addition.\n- Manifest paths are validated as portable relative paths and duplicate or unsorted entries are rejected.\n\n## Development\n\n```powershell\npython SystemExit(main())\n\n"}, "D:\\myprojects\\FileLedger\\src\\fileledger\\compare.py": {"type": "add", "content": "from __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom .manifest import FileRecord, Manifest, records_by_path\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)\nclass ChangeSet:\n    added: tuple[str, ...]\n    removed: tuple[str, ...]\n    modified: tuple[str, ...]\n    unchanged: tuple[str, ...]\n\n    @property\n    def matches(self) -> bool:\n        return not (self.added or self.removed or self.modified)\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:\n        return {\n            \"added\": list(self.added),\n            \"removed\": list(self.removed),\n            \"modified\": list(self.modified),\n            \"unchanged\": list(self.unchanged),\n            \"summary\": {\n                \"added\": len(self.added),\n                \"removed\": len(self.removed),\n                \"modified\": len(self.modified),\n                \"unchanged\": len(self.unchanged),\n            },\n        }\n\n\ndef compare_manifests(old: Manifest, new: Manifest) -> ChangeSet:\n    old_map = records_by_path(old.files)\n    new_map = records_by_path(new.files)\n\n    old_paths = set(old_map)\n    new_paths = set(new_map)\n    added = tuple(sorted(new_paths - old_paths))\n    removed = tuple(sorted(old_paths - new_paths))\n\n    modified: list[str] = []\n    unchanged: list[str] = []\n    for path in sorted(old_paths & new_paths):\n        before: FileRecord = old_map[path]\n        after: FileRecord = new_map[path]\n        if before.size != after.size or before.sha256 != after.sha256:\n            modified.append(path)\n        else:\n            unchanged.append(path)\n\n    return ChangeSet(added, removed, tuple(modified), tuple(unchanged))\n\n"}, "D:\\myprojects\\FileLedger\\src\\fileledger\\__init__.py": {"type": "add", "content": "\"\"\"FileLedger package.\"\"\"\n\n__version__ = \"0.1.0\"\n\n"}, them:\n\n```powershell\nfileledger snapshot . .\\before.json\nfileledger snapshot . .\\after.json\nfileledger diff .\\before.json .\\after.json\nfileledger verify . .\\before.json\n```\n\n`diff` and `verify` return exit code `1` when differences are found.\n\n"}, "D:\\myprojects\\FileLedger\\src\\fileledger\\cli.py": {"type": "add", "content": "from __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .compare import compare_manifests\nfrom .manifest import ManifestError, load_manifest, scan_directory, write_manifest\n\nEXIT_OK = 0\nEXIT_DIFFERENT = 1\nEXIT_USAGE_OR_INPUT = 2\n\n\ndef _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"fileledger\",\n        description=\"Create deterministic file manifests, compare them, and verify directories.\",\n    )\n    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n\n    snapshot = subparsers.add_parser(\"snapshot\", help=\"scan a directory and write a manifest\")\n    snapshot.add_argument(\"root\", type=Path, help=\"directory to scan recursively\")\n    snapshot.add_argument(\"manifest\", type=Path, help=\"output JSON manifest path\")\n\n    diff = subparsers.add_parser(\"diff\", help=\"compare two manifest files\")\n    diff.add_argument(\"old_manifest\", type=Path)\n    diff.add_argument(\"new_manifest\", type=Path)\n\n    verify = subparsers.add_parser(\"verify\", help=\"compare a directory with a historical manifest\")\n    verify.add_argument(\"root\", type=Path, help=\"directory to scan recursively\")\n    verify.add_argument(\"manifest\", type=Path, help=\"expected JSON manifest\")\n\n    return parser\n\n\ndef _print_json(value: object) -> None:\n    json.dump(value, sys.stdout, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = _parser()\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    try:\n        if args.command == \"snapshot\":\n            manifest = scan_directory(args.root)\n            write_manifest(manifest, args.manifest)\n            _print_json({\"files\": len(manifest.files), \"manifest\": str(args.manifest)})\n            return EXIT_OK\n\n        if args.command == \"diff\":\n            old = load_manifest(args.old_manifest)\n            new = load_manifest(args.new_manifest)\n            changes = compare_manifests(old, new)\n #56 · 2026-09-11T09:23:27.483Z · unknown · e_7beecda264ede963
{"type": "item_completed", "thread_id": "01a08fc3-bba4-7123-959c-a9a6af1f591d", "turn_id": "01a08fc4-055e-7fd0-a92c-160a69b4cc0b", "item": {"type": "AgentMessage", "id": "msg_aa3df749483a41ada39daa621e4495ed", "content": [{"type": "Text", "text": "已完成 FileLedger 的初版实现，当前工作区包含：\n\n- `pyproject.toml`\n- `src/fileledger/`\n  \n  - `cli.py`\n  - `manifest.py`\n  - `compare.py`\n  - `__main__.py`\n- `tests/`\n- [examples/README.md](<examples/README.md>)\n- `README.md`\n\n实现了三个子命令：\n\n```\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST\n```\n\n清单记录相对路径、文件大小、SHA-256；路径统一为 `/`，条目稳定排序，JSON 输出也使用稳定键顺序。`diff` 会区分 `added / removed / modified / unchanged`。退出码约定为：\n\n- `0`：成功且无差异\n- `1`：成功，但 `diff/verify` 检测到差异\n- `2`：输入、清单格式、文件系统或 CLI 使用错误\n\n错误输出到 `stderr`。\n\n实际验证时，系统全局 Python 环境存在一个同名旧 `fileledger` 包，最初执行：\n\nPowerShell\n\n```\npython --version\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\n得到 Python `3.13.5`，但错误导入了：\n\n```\nD:\\GoletaLabData\\src\\fileledger\n```\n\n因此我改用项目独立 Python 3.11 虚拟环境进行真实验证。最终测试结果：\n\n```\n.....                                                                    [100%]\n5 passed in 0.54s\n```\n\nCLI 帮助实际输出正常：\n\n```\nusage: fileledger [-h] {snapshot,diff,verify} ...\n\nCreate deterministic file manifests, compare them, and verify directories.\n```\n\n另外做了真实烟雾测试：\n\nPowerShell\n\n```\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\fileledger.exe snapshot .smoke .smoke_manifest.json\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\fileledger.exe verify .smoke .smoke_manifest.json\n```\n\n实际输出：\n\nJSON\n\n```\n{\n  \"files\": 1,\n  \"manifest\": \".smoke_manifest.json\"\n}\n```\n\n以及：\n\nJSON\n\n```\n{\n  \"added\": [],\n  \"modified\": [],\n  \"removed\": [],\n  \"summary\": {\n    \"added\": 0,\n    \"modified\": 0,\n    \"removed\": 0,\n    \"unchanged\": 1\n  },\n  \"unchanged\": [\n    \"a.txt\"\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nREADME 中也已经明确写出了扫描范围和限制：只处理普通文件、不跟随符号链接、不记录权限/时间戳/空目录，重命名表现为删除+新增，扫描过程中并不提供文件系统事务或锁定语义。"}], "phase": "final_answer"}, "started_at_ms": 1789118600275, "completed_at_ms": 1789118607483, "item_id": null, "call_id": null}
#57 · 2026-09-11T09:23:27.496Z · assistant_message · e_f376ed9d675b3c89
[{'type': 'output_text', 'text': '已完成 FileLedger 的初版实现，当前工作区包含：\n\n- `pyproject.toml`\n- `src/fileledger/`\n  \n  - `cli.py`\n  - `manifest.py`\n  - `compare.py`\n  - `__main__.py`\n- `tests/`\n- [examples/README.md](<examples/README.md>)\n- `README.md`\n\n实现了三个子命令：\n\n```\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST\n```\n\n清单记录相对路径、文件大小、SHA-256；路径统一为 `/`，条目稳定排序，JSON 输出也使用稳定键顺序。`diff` 会区分 `added / removed / modified / unchanged`。退出码约定为：\n\n- `0`：成功且无差异\n- `1`：成功，但 `diff/verify` 检测到差异\n- `2`：输入、清单格式、文件系统或 CLI 使用错误\n\n错误输出到 `stderr`。\n\n实际验证时，系统全局 Python 环境存在一个同名旧 `fileledger` 包，最初执行：\n\nPowerShell\n\n```\npython --version\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\n得到 Python `3.13.5`，但错误导入了：\n\n```\nD:\\GoletaLabData\\src\\fileledger\n```\n\n因此我改用项目独立 Python 3.11 虚拟环境进行真实验证。最终测试结果：\n\n```\n.....                                                                    [100%]\n5 passed in 0.54s\n```\n\nCLI 帮助实际输出正常：\n\n```\nusage: fileledger [-h] {snapshot,diff,verify} ...\n\nCreate deterministic file manifests, compare them, and verify directories.\n```\n\n另外做了真实烟雾测试：\n\nPowerShell\n\n```\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\fileledger.exe snapshot .smoke .smoke_manifest.json\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\fileledger.exe verify .smoke .smoke_manifest.json\n```\n\n实际输出：\n\nJSON\n\n```\n{\n  "files": 1,\n  "manifest": ".smoke_manifest.json"\n}\n```\n\n以及：\n\nJSON\n\n```\n{\n  "added": [],\n  "modified": [],\n  "removed": [],\n  "summary": {\n    "added": 0,\n    "modified": 0,\n    "removed": 0,\n    "unchanged": 1\n  },\n  "unchanged": [\n    "a.txt"\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nREADME 中也已经明确写出了扫描范围和限制：只处理普通文件、不跟随符号链接、不记录权限/时间戳/空目录，重命名表现为删除+新增，扫描过程中并不提供文件系统事务或锁定语义。'}]

基于你刚刚完成并测试过的 FileLedger，增量实现以下 5 项需求。请保留现有 CLI 和 JSON 默认格式，不要整库重写；每项都要修改相应模块并补充有意义的测试。

1. 增加 --exclude RELATIVE_PATH，可重复使用；拒绝绝对路径、空路径、.、.. 和越界路径，并在 snapshot 与 verify 中保持同样语义。
2. 输出文件的父目录必须已存在；禁止输出覆盖已有文件；扫描完成后才创建输出文件，写入失败时清理部分文件。
3. diff 和 verify 增加 --format json|text，默认保持 JSON；text 输出分类、数量和排序后的路径。
4. 明确拒绝符号链接、junction、reparse point 等特殊文件，不跟随也不静默跳过。
5. 补充 Unicode、空目录、二进制文件、异常输入和退出码测试，并更新 README 的实际用法和限制。

请逐项实现，运行完整测试以及必要的手工 CLI 验证，记录每条命令、实际输出和未解决问题。

from exc\r\n        if rel in seen:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"duplicate manifest path: {rel}\")\r\n        if previous is not None and rel < previous:\r\n            raise slots=True)\r\nclass ChangeSet:\r\n    added: tuple[str, ...]\r\n    removed: tuple[str, ...]\r\n    modified: tuple[str, ...]\r\n    unchanged: tuple[str, ...]\r\n\r\n    @property\r\n    def matches(self) -> bool:\r\n        return not (self.added or self.removed or self.modified)\r\n\r\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:\r\n        return {\r\n            \"added\": list(self.added),\r\n            \"removed\": list(self.removed),\r\n            \"modified\": list(self.modified),\r\n            \"unchanged\": list(self.unchanged),\r\n            \"summary\": new_paths))\r\n\r\n    modified: list[str] = []\r\n    unchanged: list[str] = []\r\n    for path in sorted(old_paths & new_paths):\r\n        before: FileRecord = old_map[path]\r\n        after: captured.out == \"\"\r\n    assert captured.err.startswith(\"fileledger: error:\")\r\n\r\n--- README ---\r\n# FileLedger\r\n\r\nFileLedger is a small local Python 3.11+ command-line tool for deterministic file inventories.\r\nIt can snapshot a directory, compare two saved manifests, and verify a current directory against a historical manifest.\r\n\r\n## Install\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e .\r\n```\r\n\r\nNo runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library are used.\r\n\r\n## Commands\r\n\r\n```text\r\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST\r\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST\r\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST\r\n```\r\n\r\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\r\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\r\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\r\n\r\n## Manifest format\r\n\r\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"files\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\r\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\r\n      \"size\": 123\r\n    }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"schema_version\": 1\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\r\n\r\n## Diff / verify output\r\n\r\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\r\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\r\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\r\n  \"summary\": {\r\n    \"added\": 1,\r\n    \"modified\": 1,\r\n    \"removed\": 1,\r\n    \"unchanged\": 2\r\n  },\r\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nErrors are written to stderr.\r\n\r\n## Exit codes\r\n\r\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\r\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\r\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\r\n\r\n## Input scope and limitations\r\n\r\n- Scans only regular files reachable beneath the supplied root.\r\n- Symbolic links are not followed or included.\r\n- File metadata other than relative path, size, and SHA-256 is intentionally ignored; permissions, owner, timestamps, ACLs, extended attributes, directories, and empty directories are not represented.\r\n- A file changed while it is being hashed can yield a snapshot reflecting the bytes observed during that read. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\r\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Renames appear as one removal plus one addition.\r\n- Manifest paths are validated as portable relative paths and duplicate or unsorted entries are rejected.\r\n\r\n## Development\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e . pytest\r\npython -m pytest -q\r\n```\r\n\r\nSee `examples/README.md` for a minimal workflow.\r\n", "stderr": "", "aggregated_output": captured.out == \"\"\r\n    assert captured.err.startswith(\"fileledger: error:\")\r\n\r\n--- README ---\r\n# FileLedger\r\n\r\nFileLedger is a small local Python 3.11+ command-line tool for deterministic file inventories.\r\nIt can snapshot a directory, compare two saved manifests, and verify a current directory against a historical manifest.\r\n\r\n## Install\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e .\r\n```\r\n\r\nNo runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library are used.\r\n\r\n## Commands\r\n\r\n```text\r\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST\r\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST\r\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST\r\n```\r\n\r\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\r\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\r\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\r\n\r\n## Manifest format\r\n\r\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"files\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\r\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\r\n      \"size\": 123\r\n    }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"schema_version\": 1\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\r\n\r\n## Diff / verify output\r\n\r\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\r\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\r\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\r\n  \"summary\": {\r\n    \"added\": 1,\r\n    \"modified\": 1,\r\n    \"removed\": 1,\r\n    \"unchanged\": 2\r\n  },\r\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nErrors are written to stderr.\r\n\r\n## Exit codes\r\n\r\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\r\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\r\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\r\n\r\n## Input scope and limitations\r\n\r\n- Scans only regular files reachable beneath the supplied root.\r\n- Symbolic links are not followed or included.\r\n- File metadata other than relative path, size, and SHA-256 is intentionally ignored; permissions, owner, timestamps, ACLs, extended attributes, directories, and empty directories are not represented.\r\n- A file changed while it is being hashed can yield a snapshot reflecting the bytes observed during that read. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\r\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Renames appear as one removal plus one addition.\r\n- Manifest paths are validated as portable relative paths and duplicate or unsorted entries are rejected.\r\n\r\n## Development\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e . pytest\r\npython -m pytest -q\r\n```\r\n\r\nSee `examples/README.md` for a minimal workflow.\r\n", "exit_code": 0, "duration": {"secs": captured.out == \"\"\r\n    assert captured.err.startswith(\"fileledger: error:\")\r\n\r\n--- README ---\r\n# FileLedger\r\n\r\nFileLedger is a small local Python 3.11+ command-line tool for deterministic file inventories.\r\nIt can snapshot a directory, compare two saved manifests, and verify a current directory against a historical manifest.\r\n\r\n## Install\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e .\r\n```\r\n\r\nNo runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library are used.\r\n\r\n## Commands\r\n\r\n```text\r\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST\r\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST\r\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST\r\n```\r\n\r\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\r\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\r\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\r\n\r\n## Manifest format\r\n\r\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"files\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\r\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\r\n      \"size\": 123\r\n    }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"schema_version\": 1\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\r\n\r\n## Diff / verify output\r\n\r\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\r\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\r\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\r\n  \"summary\": {\r\n    \"added\": 1,\r\n    \"modified\": 1,\r\n    \"removed\": 1,\r\n    \"unchanged\": 2\r\n  },\r\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nErrors are written to stderr.\r\n\r\n## Exit codes\r\n\r\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\r\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\r\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\r\n\r\n## Input scope and limitations\r\n\r\n- Scans only regular files reachable beneath the supplied root.\r\n- Symbolic links are not followed or included.\r\n- File metadata other than relative path, size, and SHA-256 is intentionally ignored; permissions, owner, timestamps, ACLs, extended attributes, directories, and empty directories are not represented.\r\n- A file changed while it is being hashed can yield a snapshot reflecting the bytes observed during that read. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\r\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Renames appear as one removal plus one addition.\r\n- Manifest paths are validated as portable relative paths and duplicate or unsorted entries are rejected.\r\n\r\n## Development\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e . pytest\r\npython -m pytest -q\r\n```\r\n\r\nSee `examples/README.md` for a minimal workflow.\r\n"}, "started_at_ms": 1789118753697, "completed_at_ms": 1789118756476, "item_id": null, "call_id": null}

captured.out == \"\"\r\n    assert captured.err.startswith(\"fileledger: error:\")\r\n\r\n--- README ---\r\n# FileLedger\r\n\r\nFileLedger is a small local Python 3.11+ command-line tool for deterministic file inventories.\r\nIt can snapshot a directory, compare two saved manifests, and verify a current directory against a historical manifest.\r\n\r\n## Install\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e .\r\n```\r\n\r\nNo runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library are used.\r\n\r\n## Commands\r\n\r\n```text\r\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST\r\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST\r\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST\r\n```\r\n\r\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\r\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\r\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\r\n\r\n## Manifest format\r\n\r\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"files\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\r\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\r\n      \"size\": 123\r\n    }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"schema_version\": 1\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\r\n\r\n## Diff / verify output\r\n\r\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\r\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\r\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\r\n  \"summary\": {\r\n    \"added\": 1,\r\n    \"modified\": 1,\r\n    \"removed\": 1,\r\n    \"unchanged\": 2\r\n  },\r\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nErrors are written to stderr.\r\n\r\n## Exit codes\r\n\r\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\r\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\r\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\r\n\r\n## Input scope and limitations\r\n\r\n- Scans only regular files reachable beneath the supplied root.\r\n- Symbolic links are not followed or included.\r\n- File metadata other than relative path, size, and SHA-256 is intentionally ignored; permissions, owner, timestamps, ACLs, extended attributes, directories, and empty directories are not represented.\r\n- A file changed while it is being hashed can yield a snapshot reflecting the bytes observed during that read. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\r\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Install\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e .\r\n```\r\n\r\nNo runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library are used.\r\n\r\n## Commands\r\n\r\n```text\r\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST [--exclude RELATIVE_PATH ...]\r\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST [--format json|text]\r\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST [--exclude RELATIVE_PATH ...] [--format json|text]\r\n```\r\n\r\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\r\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\r\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\r\n\r\n`--exclude` may be repeated. Each value names a relative file or directory subtree and uses the same semantics in `snapshot` and `verify`. Absolute paths, empty paths, `.`, `..`, and paths containing `.` / `..` segments are rejected. Backslashes are normalized to `/` after absolute-path validation.\r\n\r\n## Manifest format\r\n\r\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"files\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\r\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\r\n      \"size\": 123\r\n    }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"schema_version\": 1\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\r\n\r\n## Diff / verify output\r\n\r\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout by default, preserving the original output format:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\r\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\r\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\r\n  \"summary\": {\r\n    \"added\": 1,\r\n    \"modified\": 1,\r\n    \"removed\": 1,\r\n    \"unchanged\": 2\r\n  },\r\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse `--format text` for a human-readable form. Every category includes its count and sorted paths, for example:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nadded (1):\r\n  new.txt\r\nremoved (0):\r\nmodified (1):\r\n  changed.txt\r\nunchanged (1):\r\n  keep.txt\r\n```\r\n\r\nErrors are written to stderr.\r\n\r\n## Exit codes\r\n\r\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\r\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\r\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\r\n\r\n## Input scope and limitations\r\n\r\n- Scans ordinary directories recursively and records ordinary files only.\r\n- Symbolic links, Windows junctions/reparse points, FIFOs, sockets, devices, and other special filesystem entries are rejected with an error. They are never followed or silently skipped.\r\n- Excluded directory subtrees are pruned before inspecting entries inside them.\r\n- File metadata other than relative path, size, and SHA-256 is intentionally ignored; permissions, owner, timestamps, ACLs, extended attributes, directories, and empty directories are not represented.\r\n- The snapshot destination's parent directory must already exist. FileLedger never overwrites an existing manifest. The destination is created only after scanning succeeds; if writing fails after creation, FileLedger attempts to remove the partial output.\r\n- A file changed while it is being hashed can yield a snapshot reflecting the bytes observed during that read. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\r\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Renames appear as one removal plus one addition.\r\n- Manifest paths are validated as portable relative paths and duplicate or unsorted entries are rejected.\r\n\r\n## json|text]\r\n```\r\n\r\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\r\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\r\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\r\n\r\n`--exclude` may be repeated. Each value names a relative file or directory subtree and uses the same semantics in `snapshot` and `verify`. Absolute paths, empty paths, `.`, `..`, and paths containing `.` / `..` segments are rejected. Backslashes are normalized to `/` after absolute-path validation.\r\n\r\n## Manifest format\r\n\r\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"files\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\r\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\r\n      \"size\": 123\r\n    }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"schema_version\": 1\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\r\n\r\n## Diff / verify output\r\n\r\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout by default, preserving the original output format:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\r\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\r\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\r\n  \"summary\": {\r\n    \"added\": 1,\r\n    \"modified\": 1,\r\n    \"removed\": 1,\r\n    \"unchanged\": 2\r\n  },\r\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse `--format text` for a human-readable form. Every category includes its count and sorted paths, for example:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nadded (1):\r\n  new.txt\r\nremoved (0):\r\nmodified (1):\r\n  changed.txt\r\nunchanged (1):\r\n  keep.txt\r\n```\r\n\r\nErrors are written to stderr.\r\n\r\n## Exit codes\r\n\r\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\r\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\r\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\r\n\r\n## Input scope and limitations\r\n\r\n- Scans ordinary directories recursively and records ordinary files only.\r\n- Symbolic links, Windows junctions/reparse points, FIFOs, sockets, devices, and other special filesystem entries are rejected with an error. FileLedger never overwrites an existing manifest. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\r\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Install\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e .\r\n```\r\n\r\nNo runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library are used.\r\n\r\n## Commands\r\n\r\n```text\r\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST [--exclude RELATIVE_PATH ...]\r\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST [--format json|text]\r\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST [--exclude RELATIVE_PATH ...] [--format json|text]\r\n```\r\n\r\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\r\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\r\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\r\n\r\n`--exclude` may be repeated. Each value names a relative file or directory subtree and uses the same semantics in `snapshot` and `verify`. Absolute paths, empty paths, `.`, `..`, and paths containing `.` / `..` segments are rejected. Backslashes are normalized to `/` after absolute-path validation.\r\n\r\n## Manifest format\r\n\r\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"files\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\r\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\r\n      \"size\": 123\r\n    }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"schema_version\": 1\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\r\n\r\n## Diff / verify output\r\n\r\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout by default, preserving the original output format:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\r\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\r\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\r\n  \"summary\": {\r\n    \"added\": 1,\r\n    \"modified\": 1,\r\n    \"removed\": 1,\r\n    \"unchanged\": 2\r\n  },\r\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse `--format text` for a human-readable form. Every category includes its count and sorted paths, for example:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nadded (1):\r\n  new.txt\r\nremoved (0):\r\nmodified (1):\r\n  changed.txt\r\nunchanged (1):\r\n  keep.txt\r\n```\r\n\r\nErrors are written to stderr.\r\n\r\n## Exit codes\r\n\r\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\r\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\r\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\r\n\r\n## Input scope and limitations\r\n\r\n- Scans ordinary directories recursively and records ordinary files only.\r\n- Symbolic links, Windows junctions/reparse points, FIFOs, sockets, devices, and other special filesystem entries are rejected with an error. They are never followed or silently skipped.\r\n- Excluded directory subtrees are pruned before inspecting entries inside them.\r\n- File metadata other than relative path, size, and SHA-256 is intentionally ignored; permissions, owner, timestamps, ACLs, extended attributes, directories, and empty directories are not represented.\r\n- The snapshot destination's parent directory must already exist. FileLedger never overwrites an existing manifest. The destination is created only after scanning succeeds; if writing fails after creation, FileLedger attempts to remove the partial output.\r\n- A file changed while it is being hashed can yield a snapshot reflecting the bytes observed during that read. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\r\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Renames appear as one removal plus one addition.\r\n- Manifest paths are validated as portable relative paths and duplicate or unsorted entries are rejected.\r\n\r\n## Development\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e . pytest\r\npython -m pytest -q\r\n```\r\n\r\nSee `examples/README.md` for a minimal workflow.\r\n"}, "started_at_ms": 1789119203838, "completed_at_ms": 1789119204411, "item_id": null, "call_id": null}

\"/\")\r\n        for excluded in excludes\r\n    )\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _is_reparse_point(stat_result: os.stat_result) -> bool:\r\n    attributes = getattr(stat_result, \"st_file_attributes\", 0)\r\n    return bool(attributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT)\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _reject_special(path: Path, stat_result: os.stat_result) -> None:\r\n    if stat.S_ISLNK(stat_result.st_mode) or _is_reparse_point(stat_result):\r\n        raise ManifestError(f\"special filesystem entry is not supported: {path}\")\r\n    if not (stat.S_ISREG(stat_result.st_mode) or stat.S_ISDIR(stat_result.st_mode)):\r\n        raise ManifestError(f\"special filesystem entry is not supported: {path}\")\r\n\r\n\r\ndef scan_directory(root: Path, excludes: Iterable[str] = ()) -> Manifest:\r\n    root = root.absolute()\r\n    try:\r\n        root_stat = root.lstat()\r\n    except FileNotFoundError as exc:\r\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"input directory does not exist: {root}\") from exc\r\n    _reject_special(root, root_stat)\r\n    if not stat.S_ISDIR(root_stat.st_mode):\r\n        raise NotADirectoryError(f\"input path is not a directory: {root}\")\r\n\r\n    normalized_excludes = tuple(sorted({normalize_exclude(value) for value in excludes}))\r\n\r\n    records: list[FileRecord] = []\r\n\r\n    def walk(directory: Path) -> None:\r\n        with os.scandir(directory) as entries:\r\n            for entry in entries:\r\n                path = Path(entry.path)\r\n                relative = _portable_relative(path, root)\r\n                if _is_excluded(relative, normalized_excludes):\r\n                    continue\r\n\r\n                entry_stat = entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)\r\n                _reject_special(path, entry_stat)\r\n                if stat.S_ISDIR(entry_stat.st_mode):\r\n                    walk(path)\r\n                elif stat.S_ISREG(entry_stat.st_mode):\r\n                    records.append(\r\n                        FileRecord(\r\n                            path=relative,\r\n                            size=entry_stat.st_size,\r\n                            sha256=_sha256(path),\r\n                        )\r\n                    )\r\n\r\n    walk(root)\r\n    records.sort(key=lambda record: record.path)\r\n    return Manifest(tuple(records))\r\n\r\n\r\ndef write_manifest(manifest: Manifest, destination: Path) -> None:\r\n    parent = destination.parent\r\n    if not parent.exists():\r\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"output parent directory does not exist: {parent}\")\r\n    if not parent.is_dir():\r\n        raise NotADirectoryError(f\"output parent path is not a directory: {parent}\")\r\n    text = json.dumps(\r\n        manifest.to_dict(),\r\n        ensure_ascii=False,\r\n        indent=2,\r\n        sort_keys=True,\r\n    )\r\n    created = False\r\n    try:\r\n        with destination.open(\"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\\n\") as handle:\r\n            created = True\r\n            handle.write(text + \"\\n\")\r\n    except Exception:\r\n        if created:\r\n            try:\r\n                destination.unlink()\r\n            except FileNotFoundError:\r\n                pass\r\n        raise\r\n\r\n\r\ndef load_manifest(path: Path) -> Manifest:\r\n    try:\r\n        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\r\n    except FileNotFoundError:\r\n        raise\r\n    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:\r\n        raise ManifestError(f\"cannot read manifest {path}: {exc}\") from exc\r\n\r\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\r\n        raise ManifestError(\"manifest root must be a JSON object\")\r\n    if data.get(\"schema_version\") != SCHEMA_VERSION:\r\n        raise ManifestError(f\"unsupported schema_version: {data.get('schema_version')!r}\")\r\n    raw_files = data.get(\"files\")\r\n    if not isinstance(raw_files, list):\r\n        raise ManifestError(\"manifest 'files' must be a list\")\r\n\r\n    records: list[FileRecord] = []\r\n    previous = None\r\n    seen: set[str] = set()\r\n    for index, item in enumerate(raw_files):\r\n        if not isinstance(item, dict):\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}] must be an object\")\r\n        rel = item.get(\"path\")\r\n        size = item.get(\"size\")\r\n        sha256 = item.get(\"sha256\")\r\n        if not isinstance(rel, str) or not rel or \"\\\\\" in rel or rel.startswith(\"/\"):\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].path is not a portable relative path\")\r\n        parts = rel.split(\"/\")\r\n        if any(part in {\"\", \".\", \"..\"} for part in parts):\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].path contains invalid path segments\")\r\n        if not isinstance(size, int) or isinstance(size, bool) or size < 0:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].size must be a non-negative integer\")\r\n        if not isinstance(sha256, str) or len(sha256) != 64:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].sha256 must be a 64-character hex string\")\r\n        try:\r\n            int(sha256, 16)\r\n        except ValueError as exc:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].sha256 must be hexadecimal\") from exc\r\n        if rel in seen:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"duplicate manifest path: {rel}\")\r\n        if previous is not None and rel < previous:\r\n            raise ManifestError(\"manifest files must be sorted by path\")\r\n        seen.add(rel)\r\n        previous = rel\r\n        records.append(FileRecord(rel, size, sha256.lower()))\r\n    return Manifest(tuple(records))\r\n\r\n\r\ndef records_by_path(records: Iterable[FileRecord]) -> dict[str, FileRecord]:\r\n    return {record.path: record for record in records}\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport argparse\r\nimport json\r\nimport sys\r\nfrom pathlib import Path\r\n\r\nfrom .compare import compare_manifests\r\nfrom .manifest import ManifestError, load_manifest, normalize_exclude, scan_directory, write_manifest\r\n\r\nEXIT_OK = 0\r\nEXIT_DIFFERENT = 1\r\nEXIT_USAGE_OR_INPUT = 2\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\r\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\r\n        prog=\"fileledger\",\r\n        description=\"Create deterministic file manifests, compare them, and verify directories.\",\r\n    )\r\n    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\r\n\r\n    snapshot = subparsers.add_parser(\"snapshot\", help=\"scan a directory and write a manifest\")\r\n    snapshot.add_argument(\"root\", type=Path, help=\"directory to scan recursively\")\r\n    snapshot.add_argument(\"manifest\", type=Path, help=\"output JSON manifest path\")\r\n    snapshot.add_argument(\"--exclude\", action=\"append\", default=[], metavar=\"RELATIVE_PATH\")\r\n\r\n    diff = subparsers.add_parser(\"diff\", help=\"compare two manifest files\")\r\n    diff.add_argument(\"old_manifest\", type=Path)\r\n    diff.add_argument(\"new_manifest\", type=Path)\r\n    diff.add_argument(\"--format\", choices=(\"json\", \"text\"), default=\"json\")\r\n\r\n    verify = subparsers.add_parser(\"verify\", help=\"compare a directory with a historical manifest\")\r\n    verify.add_argument(\"root\", type=Path, help=\"directory to scan recursively\")\r\n    verify.add_argument(\"manifest\", type=Path, help=\"expected JSON manifest\")\r\n    verify.add_argument(\"--exclude\", action=\"append\", default=[], metavar=\"RELATIVE_PATH\")\r\n    verify.add_argument(\"--format\", choices=(\"json\", \"text\"), default=\"json\")\r\n\r\n    return parser\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _print_json(value: object) -> None:\r\n    json.dump(value, sys.stdout, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\r\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _print_changes(changes, output_format: str) -> None:\r\n    if output_format == \"json\":\r\n        _print_json(changes.to_dict())\r\n    else:\r\n        sys.stdout.write(changes.to_text())\r\n\r\n\r\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\r\n    parser = _parser()\r\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\r\n    try:\r\n        if args.command == \"snapshot\":\r\n            excludes = [normalize_exclude(value) for value in args.exclude]\r\n            manifest = scan_directory(args.root, excludes)\r\n            write_manifest(manifest, args.manifest)\r\n            _print_json({\"files\": len(manifest.files), \"manifest\": str(args.manifest)})\r\n            return EXIT_OK\r\n\r\n        if args.command == \"diff\":\r\n            old = load_manifest(args.old_manifest)\r\n            new = load_manifest(args.new_manifest)\r\n            changes = compare_manifests(old, new)\r\n            _print_changes(changes, args.format)\r\n            return EXIT_OK if changes.matches else EXIT_DIFFERENT\r\n\r\n        if args.command == \"verify\":\r\n            excludes = [normalize_exclude(value) for value in args.exclude]\r\n            expected = load_manifest(args.manifest)\r\n            actual = scan_directory(args.root, excludes)\r\n            changes = compare_manifests(expected, actual)\r\n            _print_changes(changes, args.format)\r\n            return EXIT_OK if changes.matches else EXIT_DIFFERENT\r\n    except (FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError, PermissionError, ManifestError, OSError) as exc:\r\n        print(f\"fileledger: error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\r\n        return EXIT_USAGE_OR_INPUT\r\n\r\n    parser.error(f\"unknown command: {args.command}\")\r\n    return EXIT_USAGE_OR_INPUT\r\n\r\n\r\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\r\n    raise SystemExit(main())\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\r\n\r\nfrom .manifest import FileRecord, Manifest, records_by_path\r\n\r\n\r\n@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)\r\nclass ChangeSet:\r\n    added: tuple[str, ...]\r\n    removed: tuple[str, ...]\r\n    modified: tuple[str, ...]\r\n    unchanged: tuple[str, ...]\r\n\r\n    @property\r\n    def matches(self) -> bool:\r\n        return not (self.added or self.removed or self.modified)\r\n\r\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:\r\n        return {\r\n            \"added\": list(self.added),\r\n            \"removed\": list(self.removed),\r\n            \"modified\": list(self.modified),\r\n            \"unchanged\": list(self.unchanged),\r\n            \"summary\": {\r\n                \"added\": len(self.added),\r\n                \"removed\": len(self.removed),\r\n                \"modified\": len(self.modified),\r\n                \"unchanged\": len(self.unchanged),\r\n            },\r\n        }\r\n\r\n    def to_text(self) -> str:\r\n        sections = (\r\n            (\"added\", self.added),\r\n            (\"removed\", self.removed),\r\n            (\"modified\", self.modified),\r\n            (\"unchanged\", self.unchanged),\r\n        )\r\n        lines: list[str] = []\r\n        for name, paths in sections:\r\n            lines.append(f\"{name} ({len(paths)}):\")\r\n            lines.extend(f\"  {path}\" for path in paths)\r\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\"\r\n\r\n\r\ndef compare_manifests(old: Manifest, new: Manifest) -> ChangeSet:\r\n    old_map = removed = tuple(sorted(old_paths - new_paths))\r\n\r\n    modified: list[str] = []\r\n    unchanged: list[str] = []\r\n    for path in sorted(old_paths & new_paths):\r\n        before: FileRecord = old_map[path]\r\n        after: FileRecord = new_map[path]\r\n        if before.size != after.size or before.sha256 != after.sha256:\r\n            modified.append(path)\r\n        else:\r\n            unchanged.append(path)\r\n\r\n    return ChangeSet(added, removed, tuple(modified), tuple(unchanged))\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport hashlib\r\nimport json\r\nfrom pathlib import \"existing\"\r\n\r\n\r\ndef test_verify_text_clean_exit_code(tmp_path: Path, capsys) -> None:\r\n    root = tmp_path / \"root\"\r\n    root.mkdir()\r\n    (root / \"x.txt\").write_text(\"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\r\n    manifest = tmp_path / \"manifest.json\"\r\n    assert main([\"snapshot\", str(root), str(manifest)]) == EXIT_OK\r\n    capsys.readouterr()\r\n    assert main([\"verify\", str(root), str(manifest), \"--format\", \"text\"]) == EXIT_OK\r\n    assert \"unchanged (1):\\n  x.txt\\n\" in capsys.readouterr().out\r\n# FileLedger\r\n\r\nFileLedger is a small local Python 3.11+ command-line tool for deterministic file inventories.\r\nIt can snapshot a directory, compare two saved manifests, and verify a current directory against a historical manifest.\r\n\r\n## Install\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e .\r\n```\r\n\r\nNo runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library are used.\r\n\r\n## Commands\r\n\r\n```text\r\nfileledger snapshot ROOT MANIFEST [--exclude RELATIVE_PATH ...]\r\nfileledger diff OLD_MANIFEST NEW_MANIFEST [--format json|text]\r\nfileledger verify ROOT MANIFEST [--exclude RELATIVE_PATH ...] [--format json|text]\r\n```\r\n\r\n`snapshot` recursively scans regular files beneath `ROOT` and writes a JSON manifest.\r\n`diff` compares two manifests and reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged paths.\r\n`verify` rescans `ROOT` and compares the result with `MANIFEST`.\r\n\r\n`--exclude` may be repeated. Each value names a relative file or directory subtree and uses the same semantics in `snapshot` and `verify`. Absolute paths, empty paths, `.`, `..`, and paths containing `.` / `..` segments are rejected. Backslashes are normalized to `/` after absolute-path validation.\r\n\r\n## Manifest format\r\n\r\nManifests are UTF-8 JSON with a stable schema:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"files\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"path\": \"docs/readme.txt\",\r\n      \"sha256\": \"...64 hex characters...\",\r\n      \"size\": 123\r\n    }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"schema_version\": 1\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach entry records the path relative to `ROOT`, byte size, and SHA-256 digest. Paths always use `/`, even on Windows. Entries are sorted lexicographically by portable relative path. JSON object keys are also sorted and output uses `\\n` line endings, so an unchanged directory produces byte-for-byte identical manifest output.\r\n\r\n## Diff / verify output\r\n\r\nBoth commands write JSON to stdout by default, preserving the original output format:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"added\": [\"new.txt\"],\r\n  \"modified\": [\"changed.txt\"],\r\n  \"removed\": [\"old.txt\"],\r\n  \"summary\": {\r\n    \"added\": 1,\r\n    \"modified\": 1,\r\n    \"removed\": 1,\r\n    \"unchanged\": 2\r\n  },\r\n  \"unchanged\": [\"keep.txt\", \"nested/stable.txt\"]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse `--format text` for a human-readable form. Every category includes its count and sorted paths, for example:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nadded (1):\r\n  new.txt\r\nremoved (0):\r\nmodified (1):\r\n  changed.txt\r\nunchanged (1):\r\n  keep.txt\r\n```\r\n\r\nErrors are written to stderr.\r\n\r\n## Exit codes\r\n\r\n- `0`: command completed and, for `diff` / `verify`, no differences were found.\r\n- `1`: `diff` / `verify` completed successfully and found one or more differences.\r\n- `2`: invalid/unreadable input, malformed manifest, filesystem error, or CLI usage error.\r\n\r\n## Input scope and limitations\r\n\r\n- Scans ordinary directories recursively and records ordinary files only.\r\n- Symbolic links, Windows junctions/reparse points, FIFOs, sockets, devices, and other special filesystem entries are rejected with an error. They are never followed or silently skipped.\r\n- Excluded directory subtrees are pruned before inspecting entries inside them.\r\n- File metadata other than relative path, size, and SHA-256 is intentionally ignored; permissions, owner, timestamps, ACLs, extended attributes, directories, and empty directories are not represented.\r\n- The snapshot destination's parent directory must already exist. FileLedger never overwrites an existing manifest. The destination is created only after scanning succeeds; if writing fails after creation, FileLedger attempts to remove the partial output.\r\n- A file changed while it is being hashed can yield a snapshot reflecting the bytes observed during that read. FileLedger does not lock files or provide filesystem-transaction semantics.\r\n- Comparison treats a file as modified when its byte size or SHA-256 differs. Renames appear as one removal plus one addition.\r\n- Manifest paths are validated as portable relative paths and duplicate or unsorted entries are rejected.\r\n\r\n## Development\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -e . pytest\r\npython -m pytest -q\r\n```\r\n\r\nSee `examples/README.md` for a minimal workflow.\r\n", "internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough": {"turn_id": "01a08fd0-36b4-7041-82d6-4771cee95620", "create_time": 1789119204.427055}, "item_id": "fco_01a08fd0-8c4b-7032-bccc-ddeddf756c9f"}

return its portable relative spelling.\"\"\"\r\n    if value == \"\":\r\n        raise ManifestError(\"exclude path must not be empty\")\r\n    if PurePosixPath(value).is_absolute() or PureWindowsPath(value).is_absolute():\r\n        raise ManifestError(f\"exclude path must be relative: {value!r}\")\r\n\r\n    portable = value.replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")\r\n    parts = \"/\".join(parts)\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _is_excluded(relative_path: str, excludes: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:\r\n    return any(\r\n        relative_path == excluded or relative_path.startswith(excluded + Manifest:\r\n    root = root.absolute()\r\n    try:\r\n        root_stat = root.lstat()\r\n    except FileNotFoundError as exc:\r\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"input directory does not exist: {root}\") from exc\r\n    _reject_special(root, root_stat)\r\n    if not stat.S_ISDIR(root_stat.st_mode):\r\n        raise NotADirectoryError(f\"input path is not a directory: {root}\")\r\n\r\n    normalized_excludes = tuple(sorted({normalize_exclude(value) for value in excludes}))\r\n\r\n    records: list[FileRecord] = []\r\n\r\n    def walk(directory: Path) -> None:\r\n        with os.scandir(directory) as entries:\r\n            for entry in entries:\r\n                path = Path(entry.path)\r\n                relative = _portable_relative(path, root)\r\n                if _is_excluded(relative, normalized_excludes):\r\n                    continue\r\n\r\n                entry_stat = entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)\r\n                _reject_special(path, entry_stat)\r\n                if stat.S_ISDIR(entry_stat.st_mode):\r\n                    walk(path)\r\n                elif stat.S_ISREG(entry_stat.st_mode):\r\n                    records.append(\r\n                        FileRecord(\r\n                            path=relative,\r\n                            size=entry_stat.st_size,\r\n                            sha256=_sha256(path),\r\n                        )\r\n                    )\r\n\r\n    walk(root)\r\n    records.sort(key=lambda record: record.path)\r\n    return text = json.dumps(\r\n        manifest.to_dict(),\r\n        ensure_ascii=False,\r\n        indent=2,\r\n        sort_keys=True,\r\n    )\r\n    created = False\r\n    try:\r\n        with destination.open(\"x\", encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\\n\") as handle:\r\n            created = True\r\n            handle.write(text + \"\\n\")\r\n    except Exception:\r\n        if created:\r\n            try:\r\n                destination.unlink()\r\n            except FileNotFoundError:\r\n                pass\r\n        raise\r\n\r\n\r\ndef load_manifest(path: Path) -> Manifest:\r\n    try:\r\n        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\r\n    except FileNotFoundError:\r\n        raise\r\n    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:\r\n        raise data.get(\"schema_version\") != SCHEMA_VERSION:\r\n        raise ManifestError(f\"unsupported schema_version: {data.get('schema_version')!r}\")\r\n    raw_files = data.get(\"files\")\r\n    if not isinstance(raw_files, list):\r\n        raise ManifestError(\"manifest 'files' must be a list\")\r\n\r\n    records: list[FileRecord] = []\r\n    previous = None\r\n    seen: set[str] = set()\r\n    for index, item in enumerate(raw_files):\r\n        if not isinstance(item, dict):\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}] must be an object\")\r\n        rel = item.get(\"path\")\r\n ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].path is not a portable relative path\")\r\n        parts = rel.split(\"/\")\r\n        if any(part in {\"\", \".\", \"..\"} for part in parts):\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].path contains invalid path segments\")\r\n        if not isinstance(size, int) or isinstance(size, bool) or size < 0:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].size must be a non-negative integer\")\r\n        if not isinstance(sha256, str) or len(sha256) != 64:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].sha256 must be a 64-character hex string\")\r\n        try:\r\n            int(sha256, 16)\r\n        except ValueError as exc:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"files[{index}].sha256 must be hexadecimal\") from exc\r\n        if rel in seen:\r\n            raise ManifestError(f\"duplicate manifest path: {rel}\")\r\n        if previous is not None and rel < previous:\r\n            raise __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport argparse\r\nimport json\r\nimport sys\r\nfrom pathlib import Path\r\n\r\nfrom .compare import compare_manifests\r\nfrom .manifest import ManifestError, load_manifest, normalize_exclude, scan_directory, write_manifest\r\n\r\nEXIT_OK = 0\r\nEXIT_DIFFERENT = 1\r\nEXIT_USAGE_OR_INPUT = 2\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\r\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\r\n        prog=\"fileledger\",\r\n        description=\"Create deterministic file manifests, compare them, and verify directories.\",\r\n    )\r\n    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\r\n\r\n    snapshot = subparsers.add_parser(\"snapshot\", help=\"scan a directory and write a manifest\")\r\n    snapshot.add_argument(\"root\", type=Path, help=\"directory to scan recursively\")\r\n    snapshot.add_argument(\"manifest\", type=Path, help=\"output JSON manifest path\")\r\n    snapshot.add_argument(\"--exclude\", type=Path)\r\n    diff.add_argument(\"new_manifest\", type=Path)\r\n    diff.add_argument(\"--format\", choices=(\"json\", \"text\"), default=\"json\")\r\n\r\n    verify = subparsers.add_parser(\"verify\", help=\"compare a directory with a historical manifest\")\r\n    verify.add_argument(\"root\", type=Path, help=\"directory to scan recursively\")\r\n    verify.add_argument(\"manifest\", type=Path, help=\"expected JSON manifest\")\r\n    verify.add_argument(\"--exclude\", action=\"append\", default=[], metavar=\"RELATIVE_PATH\")\r\n    verify.add_argument(\"--format\", choices=(\"json\", \"text\"), default=\"json\")\r\n\r\n    return parser\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _print_json(value: object) -> None:\r\n    json.dump(value, sys.stdout, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\r\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _print_changes(changes, output_format: str) -> None:\r\n    if output_format == \"json\":\r\n        _print_json(changes.to_dict())\r\n    else:\r\n        sys.stdout.write(changes.to_text())\r\n\r\n\r\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\r\n    parser = _parser()\r\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\r\n    try:\r\n        if args.command == \"snapshot\":\r\n            excludes = [normalize_exclude(value) for value in args.exclude]\r\n            manifest = scan_directory(args.root, excludes)\r\n            write_manifest(manifest, args.manifest)\r\n            _print_json({\"files\": len(manifest.files), \"manifest\": str(args.manifest)})\r\n            return EXIT_OK\r\n\r\n        if args.command == \"diff\":\r\n            old = load_manifest(args.old_manifest)\r\n            new = load_manifest(args.new_manifest)\r\n            changes = compare_manifests(old, new)\r\n            _print_changes(changes, args.format)\r\n            return EXIT_OK if changes.matches else EXIT_DIFFERENT\r\n\r\n        if args.command == \"verify\":\r\n            excludes = [normalize_exclude(value) for value in args.exclude]\r\n            expected = load_manifest(args.manifest)\r\n            actual = scan_directory(args.root, excludes)\r\n            changes = compare_manifests(expected, actual)\r\n            _print_changes(changes, args.format)\r\n            return EXIT_OK if changes.matches else EXIT_DIFFERENT\r\n    except (FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError, PermissionError, ManifestError, OSError) as exc:\r\n        print(f\"fileledger: error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\r\n        return EXIT_USAGE_OR_INPUT\r\n\r\n    parser.error(f\"unknown command: {args.command}\")\r\n    return EXIT_USAGE_OR_INPUT\r\n\r\n\r\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\r\n    raise SystemExit(main())\r\n--- tests cli ---\r\nfrom __future__ -> expected: Manifest\nmanifest.scan_directory()     -> actual: Manifest\n        ↓\ncompare.compare_manifests(expected, actual)\n        ↓\nChangeSet\n        ↓\ncli._print_changes()\n        ↓\nJSON / text + exit code 0/1\n```\n\n具体来说，cli.py 的 `_parser()` 定义了 `verify` 的 `root`、`manifest`、可重复 `--exclude` 和 `--format json|text`。进入 main() 后，`verify` 分支位于第 85 行开始。\n\n首先：\n\nPython\n\n```\nexcludes = [normalize_exclude(value) for value in args.exclude]\nexcludes.extend(_manifest_self_exclude(args.root, args.manifest))\n```\n\n`normalize_exclude()` 在 manifest.py，负责把用户排除路径转成 `/` 格式，并拒绝空路径、绝对路径、`.`、`..` 等非法段。\n\n`_manifest_self_exclude()` 在 cli.py，专门处理 manifest 自己位于 `ROOT` 内的情况。例如：\n\n```\nROOT/\n  a.txt\n  ledger.json\n```\n\n执行：\n\n```\nfileledger verify ROOT ROOT/ledger.json\n```\n\n时，它会自动产生 `ledger.json` 这个 exclude，防止历史清单文件自己被当作当前目录里的新增文件。\n\n之后：\n\nPython\n\n```\nexpected = load_manifest(args.manifest)\n```\n\n调用 manifest.py 的 `load_manifest()`。JSON 会被转换成：\n\nPython\n\n```\nManifest(\n    files=(\n        FileRecord(path=\"a.txt\", size=..., sha256=\"...\"),\n        ...\n    )\n)\n```\n\n核心数据结构是 FileRecord：\n\nPython\n\n```\nFileRecord:\n    path: str\n    size: int\n    sha256: str\n```\n\n以及 Manifest：\n\nPython\n\n```\nManifest:\n    files: tuple[FileRecord, ...]\n```\n\n`load_manifest()` 同时校验 schema、路径合法性、size、SHA-256、重复路径和排序顺序，因此 `expected` 不是未经检查的原始 JSON，而是已经验证过的 `Manifest`。\n\n接下来：\n\nPython\n\n```\nactual = scan_directory(args.root, excludes)\n```\n\n进入 manifest.py 的 `scan_directory()`。\n\n它使用 `os.scandir()` 递归目录，每个目录项先：\n\nPython\n\n```\nentry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)\n_reject_special(...)\n```\n\n所以 symlink、junction/reparse point 和其他特殊文件会在排除判断之前被拒绝。\n\n普通文件最终转换为：\n\nPython\n\n```\nFileRecord(\n    path=relative,\n    size=entry_stat.st_size,\n    sha256=_sha256(path),\n)\n```\n\n记录排序以后形成另一个 `Manifest`，也就是当前文件系统状态 `actual`。\n\n然后 cli.py 调用：\n\nPython\n\n```\nchanges = compare_manifests(expected, actual)\n```\n\n实现位于 compare.py 的 `compare_manifests()`。\n\n两个 manifest 先通过 records\\_by\\_path() 变成：\n\nPython\n\n```\nold_map = {\n    \"a.txt\": FileRecord(...),\n    ...\n}\n\nnew_map = {\n    \"a.txt\": FileRecord(...),\n    ...\n}\n```\n\n然后取路径集合：\n\nPython\n\n```\nold_paths = set(old_map)\nnew_paths = set(new_map)\n```\n\n四种结果的计算非常直接：\n\nPython\n\n```\nadded = new_paths - old_paths\nremoved = old_paths - new_paths\n```\n\n因此：\n\n- `added`：当前目录存在，历史 manifest 不存在。\n- `removed`：历史 manifest 存在，当前目录不存在。\n\n对于两边都有的路径：\n\nPython\n\n```\nfor path in sorted(old_paths & new_paths):\n```\n\n比较 `size` 和 `sha256`：\n\nPython\n\n```\nif before.size != after.size or before.sha256 != after.sha256:\n    modified.append(path)\nelse:\n    unchanged.append(path)\n```\n\n所以：\n\n- `modified`：路径相同，但 size 或 SHA-256 任一个变化。\n- `unchanged`：路径、size 和 SHA-256 均一致。\n\n最终返回 ChangeSet：\n\nPython\n\n```\nChangeSet(\n    added=(...),\n    removed=(...),\n    modified=(...),\n    unchanged=(...),\n)\n```\n\n`ChangeSet.matches` 只有在 `added`、`removed`、`modified` 全为空时才为 `True`。\n\n最后 cli.py 的 `_print_changes()` 根据 `--format` 输出：\n\nPython\n\n```\nchanges.to_dict()\n```\n\n或者：\n\nPython\n\n```\nchanges.to_text()\n```\n\nJSON 默认格式中的 `summary` 也是由 ChangeSet.to\\_dict() 根据四个 tuple 的长度即时生成的。\n\n退出码在 cli.py：\n\nPython\n\n```\nreturn EXIT_OK if changes.matches else EXIT_DIFFERENT\n```\n\n即：\n\n```\n0 = 当前目录与 manifest 一致\n1 = 存在 added / removed / modified\n2 = 输入、manifest 或文件系统异常\n```\n\n一个典型异常场景是非法排除路径：\n\n```\nfileledger verify root manifest.json --exclude ../outside\n```\n\n它在真正读取 manifest 和扫描目录之前，就会由 normalize\\_exclude() 检测到 `..` 路径段并抛出 `ManifestError`。异常最终被 cli.main() 捕获，错误写入 `stderr`：\n\n```\nfileledger: error: exclude path contains invalid path segments: '../outside'\n```\n\n并返回退出码 `2`。\n\n所以当前 `verify` 本质上是：**把历史 JSON 严格解析为 `Manifest` → 把当前目录重新扫描为同一种 `Manifest` → 按路径集合和 size/SHA-256 做确定性比较 → 输出 `ChangeSet`。**"}], "phase": "final_answer"}, "started_at_ms": 1789119968557, "completed_at_ms": 1789119989713, "item_id": null, "call_id": null}
